analysis.title: How to invest in AI amid AI spending worries?
key_insights: Investors are focusing on whether AI spending produces revenue, profits and cash flow, rather than rewarding higher investment by itself.
UBS says strong cloud growth and continued demand for computing capacity support its view that AI investment will remain a positive driver of global equity returns in 2027.
The recent technology sell-off reflects a shift in the AI debate from how much companies spend to how the spending is financed and whether it earns adequate returns.

Some major technology companies reported negative quarterly free cash flow as investment rose, and more indebted specialist computing infrastructure providers came under pressure over their funding models.
UBS raised its aggregate AI capital-spending forecasts to USD 1.0tr in 2026, USD 1.4tr in 2027 and USD 1.5tr in 2028, concentrated among large platforms with strong balance sheets.

The market is separating companies with healthy finances, pricing power and visible demand from those that depend on borrowing or need consistently high infrastructure utilization, so UBS expects wider gaps between AI leaders and laggards.

UBS advises reviewing whether AI has become a larger share of the portfolio than intended, since holdings concentrated in one or two names are more exposed to earnings misses, weaker guidance and regulatory changes.
Diversification across the AI value chain covers chip makers, cloud capacity, software, electricity and cooling suppliers for data centers, power grid upgrades and AI adopters.
UBS prefers high-quality companies with reasonable valuations, strong finances and less exposure to excess capacity, including select semiconductor manufacturing, computing and power names.
UBS suggests looking beyond the US: Asia for semiconductors and memory, and European industrial and technology companies for power systems, automation, electrification and data center infrastructure.
Outside tech, UBS prefers industrials, health care and financials, and regionally the Eurozone, emerging markets and Asia ex-Japan on a relative basis.

For volatility, UBS describes capital preservation structures for investors wanting recovery exposure with some downside protection at maturity, and reverse convertibles for higher-risk investors willing to own the stock at the specified price.

sector_views.rationale: Preferred equity sector, with European industrials seen benefiting from AI-related spending on power systems, automation and electrification.
Preferred equity sector to add earnings growth sources and reduce reliance on the technology cycle.
Preferred equity sector to add earnings growth sources and reduce reliance on the technology cycle.
AI investment remains a positive driver of 2027 equity returns, but UBS wants diversification across the AI value chain and quality, with less exposure to excess capacity and heavily indebted names.

earnings_insights: Some major technology companies reported negative quarterly free cash flow as investment increased, per the latest results (the report does not name the companies or give figures).
Latest results showed strong cloud growth and continued demand for computing capacity (no figures given).

macro_indicators.interpretation: UBS raised its forecast after the latest results showed strong demand.
Spending is concentrated among large technology platforms with strong balance sheets.
Spending growth continues but at a slower pace than in 2027.

trade_ideas.description: Capital preservation structured product on AI-linked stocks for exposure to a recovery with some or all of the initial investment protected at maturity
trade_ideas.rationale: The investor accepts limits on potential gains in exchange for a degree of loss limitation.
trade_ideas.risk: Depends on the issuer being able to repay, usually applies only at maturity, and does not necessarily prevent losses if sold early.

trade_ideas.description: Reverse convertible on a stock the investor is willing to own, to generate income from elevated volatility
trade_ideas.rationale: The investor receives a coupon while using elevated market volatility to generate income.
trade_ideas.risk: The investor may be repaid in shares if the underlying falls sufficiently, which can result in substantial losses.

risk_factors: Higher AI spending does not guarantee strong investment returns.
Negative free cash flow at major technology companies as investment increases.
Funding and debt pressure on more indebted specialist computing infrastructure providers.
Companies that need consistently high infrastructure utilization to meet obligations.
Concentration in one or two successful technology companies exposes portfolios to disappointing earnings, weaker guidance, regulatory changes or shifts in investor expectations.
Structured strategies carry issuer, pricing, liquidity and capital-loss risks and have less intuitive payoffs.
vol_and_positioning: Large price swings can create opportunities to rebalance, add exposure, generate income and manage potential losses, depending on the investor's goal.
Capital preservation structures limit potential gains in exchange for some loss limitation, depend on issuer repayment, usually apply only at maturity, and may not prevent losses if sold early.
Reverse convertibles use elevated volatility to pay a coupon, but the investor may be repaid in shares if the underlying falls enough, which can cause substantial losses.
